name: A7A5
oneLiner: A7A5 is Old Vector's RUB stablecoin backed by an undisclosed mix of ruble deposits and short-term assets; its issuer network faces OFAC, EU, and UK sanctions.
collateral: An undisclosed Russian-ruble reserve basket that issuer materials variously describe as deposits and as deposits plus short-term assets; current constituent weights, institutions, custody, and assurance evidence are unavailable
pegMechanism: Fiat-backed 1:1 peg to the Russian ruble enforced exclusively via off-chain primary-market mint and redemption with KYC-verified authorized partners (e.g. a7a5.kg for Russian-account holders depositing or withdrawing RUB); no on-chain DEX-based RUB liquidity exists, so USD-denominated price prints reflect RUB/USD spot movements rather than secondary-market arbitrage; since 2026-02-09 the issuer (Old Vector LLC) distributes nearly all overnight reserve income to holders as additional A7A5 using a formula of the Central Bank of Russia key rate minus 1 percentage point, recalculated when the key rate changes

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: A7A5's issuer publishes exact Ethereum and Tron contracts and describes issuance on both networks. No independent bridge or active CEX-based bridge was evidenced, so both routes are treated as issuer-native minting.

jurisdiction.license: VASP license (Law on Virtual Assets No. 12, 2022); issuer: Old Vector LLC

mintAuthority.summary: A7A5 is issued by Old Vector LLC; minting and redemption run off-chain through KYC-gated authorized partners against RUB deposits. On-chain, the Ethereum token's issue() function is owned by a 3-of-5 custom multisig (5 EOA signers), and the Tron token's owner is a 3-of-5 Multisig contract (5 EOA signers). Both tokens are direct immutable deployments with no proxy or other mint-logic upgrade path.

controls.label: Old Vector LLC issuance backend
controls.evidence: Issuer-operated primary-market mint/redeem: Old Vector LLC creates A7A5 supply against custodied RUB bank deposits via KYC-verified partners (e.g. a7a5.kg); no on-chain permissionless mint exists.

controls.label: A7A5 ETH token owner (custom 3-of-5 multisig)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25526129 (2026-07-13), owner() on A7A5 Ethereum (0x6fa0be17e4bea2fcfa22ef89bf8ac9aab0ab0fc9) returns 0x7d2d47e441915ff9c2d5a6e4a7aadd5e02722e29. That contract has getOwners() returning the same 5 EOA addresses (0x6dab4c10..., 0xae8dd5dd..., 0x8b04bdc0..., 0x99d3df8c..., 0x3353d63a...) and getThreshold()=3. The token's EIP-1967 implementation and beacon slots are zero; its exact-block runtime hash is 0x762de09de4267df1038313af242dd978f2835d193d90a51de836e808eae57dc9. No modules or guard were detected on the owner multisig.

controls.label: A7A5 Tron token owner (3-of-5 multisig)
controls.evidence: At Tron block 83506136 (2026-06-11): owner() on A7A5 Tron (TLeVfrdym8RoJreJ23dAGyfJDygRtiWKBZ) returns TML1DbrPXYDDwatGxw66iEwECnXCG54uJy, which is a Tron Multisig contract. getOwners() returns 5 owner hex addresses; getThreshold()=3. All 5 owner addresses resolve as non-contract EOAs on Tron.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25526129 (2026-07-13), the A7A5 token owner remains the custom 3-of-5 multisig with the same five EOA owners. The verified Ethereum source declares owner, compliance, and accountant as constructor-set immutable values, exposes no upgrade function, and the implementation and beacon slots are zero. On Tron, the independently deployed A7A5 runtime exposes the same direct token interface; Tronscan reports it fully verified and non-proxy, and opcode inspection of the 12,955-byte executable region found no DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE, or SELFDESTRUCT path. The Tron owner was previously confirmed at block 83506136 as a 3-of-5 multisig with five EOA owners. The issuer-backend control cannot be independently confirmed from chain state, but both addressable on-chain mint surfaces and both immutable token runtimes are resolved.

notices.title: Multi-jurisdiction sanctions exposure
notices.message: A7A5 and related infrastructure are subject to major sanctions risk. OFAC designated Grinex and A7-linked entities in August 2025, and the A7A5 token, issuer network, and venues such as Grinex/TengriCoin have also been targeted by EU and UK sanctions actions tied to Russian sanctions-evasion infrastructure.
